rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 was REVISE on a gating HIGH from editquality. Every objection is answered below by a measurement or by code; none by argument.

THE GATING HIGH — 'the sketch keys the map on dark_section while everything refers to dark_section_audit; if the key is wrong this edit is a silent no-op'. This was the right question to ask and it is answerable at the data, not from the code. `category` and `item_type` are different fields (designItemTypes maps the first to the second). [MEASURED 2026-08-19, archive-inclusive] every one of the 30 rows of this type carries spec.category = 'dark_section' AND handler_agent = 'color-variable-fixer'. So the key is not merely live — it is demonstrably the key that produced the routing this change corrects. A dead key could not have set that column on 30 rows.

THE TWO MEDIUMS, which are the same objection from two seats and were both right: editquality — 'a comment-only change... the precondition it records is enforced by nobody'; architecture — 'the roster/routing sync gap has no structural guard, only a comment'. Fixed rather than noted. noChangeRule gains MeasuredAgainstHandler (the handler its CounterPaths were measured against) and LicenceVoided, and a new test pins the pair ACROSS the two files that were previously unconnected. The invariant is deliberately NOT 'these must always agree': that would forbid the legitimate window between fixing a routing and being able to measure the new handler, which cannot be closed until that handler has actually run the type. It is: THEY AGREE, OR THE ENTRY DECLARES THAT THEY DO NOT AND NAMES THE NEW HANDLER. An entry may be stale, but only out loud. Mutation-proven: deleting LicenceVoided turns it RED ('now routes to css-patch-agent, and the entry does not say so'); making LicenceVoided name the wrong handler turns it RED ('does not name the handler now routed'); control green, restored byte-identical.

GUARDIAN'S MEDIUM, the same challenge from the routing side ('a routing fix aimed at a dead key changes nothing while looking fixed'), is answered by the same 30-row measurement above. Its low about where the warning is PLACED is answered by the new test: placement now matters less, because the invariant is checked at build time rather than depending on the next author reading a comment in the right file.

REUSE_AGENT'S MISSING, which was the most substantive thing raised and which I had not checked: 'no confirmation that css-patch-agent's plan_css_fix step can actually emit an ADDITIVE scoped block rather than only patching existing declarations — the 39 deploys prove it writes styles.css, not that it produces the --section-* pattern this category needs.' Fair. Read the live prompt. It is append-only BY CONSTRUCTION: 'Write ONLY the new or overriding CSS rules that implement the fix described in the audit finding. The platform APPENDS your rules to the END of the stylesheet above — you never return the stylesheet itself, and you cannot delete or edit existing rules.' It cannot do anything BUT emit an additive block, and it already consumes spec.category, spec.description, spec.suggestion, spec.affected_component and spec.page_name — every one of which these items carry. ⚠ One nuance found in the same read and stated rather than hidden: the prompt instructs 'only use var(--x) names that are DEFINED in the stylesheet above; otherwise use literal values'. These findings ask the agent to DEFINE new custom properties, which is a declaration rather than a reference and is unaffected — but a finding that asks it to REFERENCE an undefined token will get a literal instead. That is a safeguard, not a defect, and it is the honest limit of the capability claim.

REUSE_AGENT'S LOW about two agents owning adjacent dark-mode repair: accepted as a real watch item and recorded. color-variable-fixer retains hardcoded_section_colors, which is a genuinely different job (a site-level aggregate over hex literals inside component bodies, with its own registered verifier and Grades remit test) — not a fork of this one. If the two ever converge on one defect class they should be unified rather than left to calcify.

Unchanged from round 1: the measurements, the risk statement about bugs_open/198, and the blast radius (designRouting is read at FILING time; no existing row is re-routed; both carriers are off so the route is inert).

plan.summary: Route the dark_section design-audit category to css-patch-agent, which can write the scoped CSS the findings ask for, instead of color-variable-fixer, whose transform provably cannot — and record at both sites that gate 1b's roster entry for the type is thereby unlicensed until re-measured.

edits.rationale: ROUND 2, answering editquality's and architecture's mediums. Two fields that let a roster entry state the handler its CounterPaths were measured against, and declare — out loud — when the live routing has moved away from it. Without them the staleness is invisible to everything except a human reading a comment.

edits.rationale: The invariant itself, spanning the two previously-unconnected files. Deliberately NOT 'these must always agree' — that forbids the legitimate window between fixing a routing and being able to measure the new handler. It is: they agree, OR the entry declares they do not AND names the new handler. Silent staleness becomes unrepresentable; honest staleness stays legal. Mutation-proven both ways.

grounded_in: The live suggestions this type carries, verbatim from spec->>'suggestion': "Add a scoped style block for .cta-section that defines --section-text: #ffffff; --section-text-muted: rgba(255,255,255,0.75)..." and "Add a .site-footer scoped block defining --section-text, --section-heading, --section-surface, and --section-bg using the dark surface...". Additive stylesheet rules, not hex substitution.

check_hardcoded_section_colors.go's own header on the transform being replaced: "background with single dark hex -> var(--color-primary)", "gradient with two dark hex values -> gradient with var(--color-primary), var(--color-secondary)" — the complete output alphabet.
MEASURED 2026-08-19, archive-inclusive: dark_section_audit has 26 complete + 4 failed across 17 sites, and count of completions reporting a non-zero response.fix_result.total_fixed is ZERO.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: css-patch-agent's completed items include 39 whose response.css_deployed is a git-adapter success deploying assets/css/styles.css (commit messages 'CSS fix: contrast (theme v2..v5)'), most recent 2026-08-18 — capability confirmed at the artefact, not inferred from its workflow config.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: webdesign-agent has 1,268 completed needs_design_review items and ALL of them carry an empty response envelope, which is why it was rejected as the target despite taking every other colour category.

MEASURED 2026-08-19: css-patch-agent's reply shape carries css_fix / css_deployed and 56 of 103 completions carry no response envelope at all — there is NO numeric counter in its shape, which is why gate 1b's CounterPaths for this type cannot simply be repointed.

bugs_open/198's own status, on the risk of routing more work at this agent: candidate 1 LIVE (migration 318 applied + verified), candidate 3 LIVE at the pod (chassis v1.0.1277, both replicas pod-grepped 2026-08-10), and its last commit records that 'only the witnessed run keeps 198 open'. 98 completions since, no recurrence.

MEASURED 2026-08-19, answering the gating HIGH at the data rather than the code: all 30 dark_section_audit rows (archive-inclusive) carry spec.category='dark_section' AND handler_agent='color-variable-fixer'. The key being edited is the key that set that column, so it cannot be a dead-key no-op.

css-patch-agent's LIVE plan_css_fix prompt_template, answering reuse_agent's capability doubt: 'Write ONLY the new or overriding CSS rules... The platform APPENDS your rules to the END of the stylesheet above — you never return the stylesheet itself, and you cannot delete or edit existing rules.' Append-only by construction, and it already reads spec.category/description/suggestion/affected_component/page_name.

The same prompt's limit, stated rather than hidden: 'Only use var(--x) names that are DEFINED in the stylesheet above; otherwise use literal values.' Defining a new --section-* property is unaffected; referencing an undefined one yields a literal.

Mutation matrix for the new invariant, on a clean git archive HEAD overlay with an unmutated control and byte-identical restore: LicenceVoided deleted -> RED; LicenceVoided naming the wrong handler -> RED.
